{{italic title}}
{{Short description|Refuted conjecture of geometric topology}}
The '''''Hauptvermutung'''''{{efn|[[German language|German]] for ''main [[conjecture]]''. It is an abbreviation for '''''die Hauptvermutung der kombinatorischen Topologie''''', which translates as ''the main conjecture of [[combinatorial topology]]''.}} of [[geometric topology]] is a now refuted conjecture asking whether any two [[Triangulation (topology)|triangulations]] of a [[triangulable space]] have subdivisions that are combinatorially equivalent, i.e. the subdivided triangulations are built up in the same combinatorial pattern. It was originally formulated as a conjecture in 1908 by [[Ernst Steinitz]]<ref>{{cite journal |first=E. |last=Steinitz |title=Beiträge zur Analysis situs |journal=Sitz-Ber. Berlin Math. Ges. |volume=7 |date=1908 |pages=29–49}}</ref> and [[Heinrich Franz Friedrich Tietze]],<ref>{{cite journal |first=H. |last=Tietze |title=Über die topologischen Invarianten mehrdimensionaler Mannigfaltigkeiten |journal= Monatshefte für Mathematik und Physik|volume=19 |date=1908 |pages=1–118 |doi=10.1007/BF01736688|s2cid=120998023 |url=https://zenodo.org/record/2024013 }}</ref> but it is now known to be false.

==History==
The non-[[manifold]] version was disproved by [[John Milnor]] in 1961 using [[Analytic torsion|Reidemeister torsion]].<ref>{{Cite journal|first=John W.|last= Milnor |authorlink=John Milnor| title=Two complexes which are homeomorphic but combinatorially distinct|journal= [[Annals of Mathematics]] |volume=74|year=1961|issue= 2 |pages=575–590|mr=133127|doi=10.2307/1970299|jstor=1970299}}</ref>

The manifold version is true in [[dimension]]s <math>m\le 3</math>. The cases <math>m = 2</math> and <math>3</math> were proved by [[Tibor Radó]] and [[Edwin E. Moise]] in the 1920s and 1950s, respectively.<ref>{{cite journal | last = Radó | first = Tibor | authorlink=Tibor Radó| title = Über den Begriff der Riemannschen Fläche | journal= Acta Scientarum Mathematicarum Universitatis Szegediensis | volume=2 | year=1925 | issue = 1 | pages=96–114|jfm=51.0273.01}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last = Moise | first = Edwin E. |authorlink=Edwin E. Moise| title = Affine structures in 3-manifolds. V. The triangulation theorem and Hauptvermutung | journal= [[Annals of Mathematics]] | volume=56 | year=1952 | issue = 2 | pages=101–121 | doi=10.2307/1969769| jstor = 1969769 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book | last = Moise | first = Edwin E. | title = Geometric Topology in Dimensions 2 and 3 | year = 1977 | isbn = 978-0-387-90220-3 }}</ref>

An obstruction to the manifold version was formulated by [[Andrew Casson]] and [[Dennis Sullivan]] in 1967–69 (originally in the [[simply-connected]] case), using the [[Rochlin invariant]] and the [[cohomology group]] <math>H^3(M;\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})</math>.

In dimension <math>m \ge 5</math>, a [[homeomorphism]] <math>f \colon N \to M</math> of ''m''-dimensional [[piecewise linear manifold]]s has an [[Kirby-Siebenmann class|invariant]] <math>\kappa(f) \in H^3(M;\Z/2\Z)</math> such that <math>f</math> is [[Homotopy#Isotopy|isotopic]] to a piecewise linear (PL) homeomorphism [[if and only if]] <math>\kappa(f) = 0</math>. In the simply-connected case and with <math>m \ge 5</math>, <math>f</math> is [[homotopic]] to a PL homeomorphism if and only if <math>[\kappa(f)] = 0 \in [M,G/{\rm PL}]</math>.

This quantity <math>\kappa(f)</math> is now seen as a relative version of the triangulation obstruction of [[Robion Kirby]] and [[Laurent C. Siebenmann]], obtained in 1970. The [[Kirby–Siebenmann obstruction]] is defined for any [[Compact space|compact]] ''m''-dimensional topological manifold ''M''
:<math>\kappa(M)\in H^4(M;\Z/2\Z)</math>
again using the Rochlin invariant. For <math>m\ge  5</math>, the manifold ''M'' has a [[PL structure]] (i.e., it can be triangulated by a PL manifold) if and only if <math>\kappa(M) = 0</math>, and if this obstruction is 0, the PL structures are parametrized by <math>H^3(M;\Z/2\Z)</math>. In particular there are only a finite number of essentially distinct PL structures on ''M''.

For compact simply-connected manifolds of dimension 4, [[Simon Donaldson]] found examples with an infinite number of inequivalent PL structures, and [[Michael Freedman]] found the [[E8 manifold]] which not only has no PL structure, but (by work of Casson) is not even homeomorphic to a [[simplicial complex]].<ref>{{cite book | last1 = Akbulut | first1 = Selman |authorlink1=Selman Akbulut| last2 = McCarthy | first2 = John D. | title = Casson's invariant for oriented homology 3-spheres | url = https://archive.org/details/cassonsinvariant0000akbu | url-access = registration | publisher = [[Princeton University Press]] | year = 1990 | isbn = 0-691-08563-3 | mr = 1030042}}</ref>

In 2013, [[Ciprian Manolescu]] proved that there exist compact topological manifolds of dimension 5 (and hence of any dimension greater than 5) that are not homeomorphic to a simplicial complex.<ref>{{cite journal |first=Ciprian |last=Manolescu |authorlink=Ciprian Manolescu| orig-year=2015 |title=Pin(2)-equivariant Seiberg–Witten Floer homology and the Triangulation Conjecture |journal=[[Journal of the American Mathematical Society]] |volume=29 |year=2016 |pages=147–176 |doi=10.1090/jams829|arxiv=1303.2354 |s2cid=16403004 }}</ref> Thus Casson's example illustrates a more general phenomenon that is not merely limited to dimension 4.
